## Natural history notes

A tiny dragonfly characterized by its amber-tinted wings, short orange-brown body, and fluttery, wasp-like flight over the water. In Florida, the Eastern Amberwing is common around ponds, lakes, marshes, canals, ditches, stormwater basins, and slow wetland edges with sunny perches and emergent vegetation. Adults hunt small flying insects from low stems or shoreline plants, while the aquatic nymphs live among submerged vegetation and bottom debris where they prey on tiny aquatic animals.
